headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from shared-bus Pipecat feeding Cognee’s memory/workflow stack; no direct evidence of a blocking isolation layer.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Pipecat uses a shared bus and can carry text/conversation state, while Cognee ingests documents, workflows, and decisions with session memory. That creates a plausible default path where attacker-controlled content from B is treated as trusted input by A. No explicit provenance or isolation mechanism is documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Pipecat routes user-supplied text into Cognee without provenance tags, injection is reachable.
IF Cognee parses shared-bus content as instructions or workflow state, the risk materializes.
mitigations: Add provenance labels to all B→A messages.
Filter/strip instruction-like text before A ingests B output.
Separate the shared bus into per-session channels.
Review one end-to-end message path for prompt-like payloads.
requires-engineering: enforce schema validation on all inter-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cognee touches personal data, finance data, support history, and documents; Pipecat can process text, conversation state, and send data to multiple third-party STT/LLM/TTS APIs. If they share a workspace or bus, sensitive A-side data can flow into B-side API calls by default. The profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF A and B share a workspace, B may ingest A-side sensitive files or state.
IF B forwards conversation text to external STT/LLM/TTS providers, leaked content leaves the pair.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces.
Disable external API providers in B for sensitive sessions.
Minimize A-side data passed into B to redacted summaries.
Audit one sample transcript for sensitive-field leakage.
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before any B egress.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has session-memory and multiple instances; B has a shared bus and multiple instances. Even without explicit filesystem write scopes, both can mutate shared conversational state or downstream resources, so concurrent writes can conflict. Because no locking or coordination primitive is documented, the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same shared bus topic, state races can occur.
IF an orchestrator fans out multiple instances without locks, updates can overwrite each other.
mitigations: Assign separate bus topics per agent.
Serialize writes for shared conversation state.
Check for duplicate updates in one test run.
Limit one writer per resource at a time.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency/version checks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Pipecat can emit text and conversation state, and Cognee stores decisions, workflows, and successful implementations. That makes it plausible that B’s output becomes A’s authoritative memory or that A’s output is reused by B without verification. No documented verification step appears in either profile, so cascading mistakes are a default-path concern.
conditions: IF B forwards generated text into A’s memory layer, errors can persist.
IF A’s stored outputs are later rendered or acted on by B, mistakes cascade.
mitigations: Require human review before persisting B output in A.
Mark B-generated content as untrusted metadata.
Add a verification step before downstream actions.
Sample one stored record for hallucinated facts.
requires-engineering: implement confidence/provenance gating.

E_compliance.rationale: A explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while B can route text and conversation state through many third-party APIs. That creates a compliance mismatch risk around retention, residency, and processor obligations if regulated data is sent through B. The profiles do not document matching controls, so medium is the conservative choice.
conditions: IF regulated A-side data is sent through B providers, processor and residency obligations may be triggered.
IF B logs conversation state longer than A’s policy allows, retention mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Block regulated data from B by policy.
Review provider residency for one configured B backend.
Set the shortest practical retention in B.
Document which data classes may cross the boundary.
requires-engineering: align DPA, retention, and deletion workflows.
